description: Authored map for scripts/ai-in-biology-admission.ts: which pack records each part admits, how each is corrected under the maintainer’s decisions of 2026-10-30 (review/ai-in-biology-pack-2026-10-30.md) and the cross-family check of 2026-10-30, the records held with their reasons, and the records, documents, entities and sources added at admission. Records outside both parts’ include lists are not admitted.

1.snapshotDescription: Dataset state before part 1 of the AI in biology admission (2026-10-31): the IDs it adds and the rows it changes as they were.
1.scope: On 2026-10-31, by the maintainer’s decisions of 2026-10-30 and the corrections of a blind cross-family check, the first part of a machine-prepared, machine-audited candidate pack on AI in biology was admitted: the institutions and programmes (DeepMind and Google DeepMind’s science work, Isomorphic Labs, EvolutionaryScale, Arc Institute, the Institute for Protein Design, Microsoft Research AI for Science, NVIDIA BioNeMo and drug-discovery companies), the models, papers and resources (CASP, AlphaFold, the AlphaFold database, AlphaMissense, AlphaProteo, RoseTTAFold, RFdiffusion, ESM, Evo, Rosetta and Foldit) and the people credited with them, each recorded as what a dated document states. A paper’s contribution is its authors’ statement; CASP results are the organisers’ statements; a company’s statement of purpose, funding, a trial or a result is the company’s, never an independent finding. All records are seeds; none is human-reviewed.

2.snapshotDescription: Dataset state before part 2 of the AI in biology admission (2026-10-31): the IDs it adds and the rows it changes as they were.
2.scope: In part 2, schema 2.23 adds two predicates, an announced partnership and an announced award, each recorded as the announcing party states it: an announced partnership is not a contract performed and an “up to” amount is not a payment. The claims strand records six propositions about AI and biology with the texts that articulate, contest or bear on them, in the collection “AI in science”, whose first section is biology. A record of a text’s stance on a proposition is never evidence that the proposition is true. All records are seeds; none is human-reviewed.

aib-arg-p1-lyu-2024.statement: Lyu et al. (Science, published online 16 May 2024) report that prospective docking against unrefined AlphaFold2 models of two receptors gave hit rates similar to docking against experimental structures, and state that such models remain relevant for ligand discovery, extending the domain of structure-based drug design.

aib-arg-p6-jayatunga-2024.qualification: The record documents what this text states, in its register; it is not evidence that the proposition is true and implies no influence on or from any other text. Quoted from the Europe PMC record of the abstract. The cross-family machine check of 2026-10-30 read the main text through an author-uploaded copy relayed by a web reader (the publisher’s text and supplementary tables were not retrieved): as of December 2023 the authors count 21 successes among 24 completed phase I trials and four among ten phase II trials. Their comparison is with historical averages, not a matched one, on a small, selected sample of molecules from AI-native companies, and discontinuations for commercial reasons constrain the reading. The record states the authors’ rate statement with those caveats; it is not evidence that AI caused a higher rate (maintainer decision of 2026-10-30). Earliest located for this proposition among the texts found by the searches described under “How we searched”; not a claim that no earlier text exists.

thought.qualifier: Challenges the present performance of the tested models; not a contradiction of the proposition as a whole.

aib-arg-p2-ahlmann-eltze-2025.qualification: The record documents what this text states, in its register; it is not evidence that the proposition is true and implies no influence on or from any other text. A qualified challenge: the paper reports that the models it tested did not outperform deliberately simple baselines on its benchmarks, and concludes that a stated goal of such models is still elusive. It challenges the present performance of those models; it does not contradict the proposition as a whole, which does not require outperforming simple baselines and includes models that will be able to predict cell behaviour (cross-family check, item B119; maintainer decision of 2026-10-30).

newClaims.qualification: The record documents what this text states, in its register; it is not evidence that the proposition is true and implies no influence on or from any other text. A proposed model of one signalling pathway, not a simulation of a whole cell; the criterion covers a cell’s responses, and the cross-family check applied its “machine-learning or other AI model” to a PDP (neural) network. The research pack had headlined a 2018 text; this one holds the role from the admission (maintainer decision of 2026-10-30). thought.qualifier: A proposed network model of a signalling pathway, not of a whole cell.
